artifacts.summary: Research for all three folded phases: Phase 1 well-formedness check design (validate-artifact.sh, advisory, newline-flattened matching), both ALSO-SETTLE rulings (resolve-check and mark-owed detection both excluded with corpus evidence), Phase 2 Part A/B + further B-case designs, and Phase 3 enumeration-completeness design.

memory_candidates.content: When validating a fixed-case literal bracket-delimited token (e.g. `[TOKEN: source]`) that may legitimately span multiple markdown source lines, a per-line `grep -E` recall-misses any occurrence whose closing bracket is on a later line -- this is the same failure class that sank a prior general carried-figure-contradiction detector (markdown bold splitting a literal trigger phrase). Fix: flatten newlines (e.g. `tr '\n' ' '`) before matching with `[^]]*\]`, which also passes markdown emphasis and table pipes through for free since neither is a `]` character.

scripts/validate-artifact.sh has a reusable advisory-first idiom for a new per-artifact well-formedness check: log_warn only (never log_error) in default mode, gated by artifact_type, with an explicit comment stating the promotion-to-error criterion -- modeled on the existing per-phase Verification Tier and Files-to-modify checks. --strict already folds warnings into the exit-affecting total for free; no new --strict wiring needed.
